- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 10+ consecutive days show price decline, forecast should trend upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversal signal.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is flat, model often predicts continuation; if no clear trend, use 20-day SMA or 30-day moving average as anchor.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply 1–2% downward bias for first 5 days if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply 1–2% downward correction at shift point, then revert to trend if sentiment stabilizes.
